chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked, while I was present, about a man who became junub in his garment and then sweats in it. He said: “I do not see any harm in it.” He said: Indeed, he sweats so much that if he wished to wring it, he could wring it out. He said: Then Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام frowned in the man’s face and said: “If you insist, then sprinkle some water on it.”

key_terms.أَجْنَبَ: entered the state of janabah (major ritual impurity)
key_terms.بَأْسًا: harm, problem, or objection in legal context

ai.seo_question: Is a garment worn in the state of janabah made najis by sweat?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on a garment worn by a person in the state of janabah when he sweats in it. Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام states that there is no problem with it, and when the questioner persists, he instructs him to sprinkle some water on it.
